$comment: pe UCRT migration Phase 1 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the pe `library` binding moved msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll. P1 flips only the STATELESS descriptors — the migration's safe unit is a CO-STATE GROUP (a heap ptr / FILE* / CRT fd / errno / static tm created by one CRT and read by the other corrupts SILENTLY), and a ctype classifier neither creates nor consumes any such object: it maps a value to a value. All 13 symbols verified present in the live ucrtbase.dll export table (objdump -p) per the EAGER-IMPORT LAW (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT: DSS imports EVERY declared shipped extern whether referenced or not, so an absent name breaks the binary LOAD with 0xC0000139). ★ LOCALE IS THE NON-OBVIOUS RISK HERE, and it was PROVEN not asserted: every ctype classifier consults the CRT's current locale (UCRT's __acrt_locale_data), which is normally populated by the EXE's UCRT startup that DSS's startup-less pe entry does NOT run — an unpopulated table would make isalpha() silently answer wrong (a silent-miscompile class). The Phase-0 pre-flight ran a pe64 --config=release binary bound to ucrtbase.dll asserting the exact C-locale answers in BOTH directions (isalpha('A')/isdigit('7')/isspace('\t')/isupper/islower/ispunct positive AND isalpha('4')/isdigit('x')/isupper('k') negative, plus toupper/tolower mappings): ucrtbase's locale data self-initializes on DLL-attach and every answer is correct. Same run under msvcrt.dll for contrast — identical. See math.json for the first ucrtbase binding (C99 math, Phase-0-of-record).
